headline: Epoch AI found that a quarter of new math papers now say they used AI, up from 4% in April.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the analysis was published on 18 Sep 2026, so it is not new today.
importance_line: It gives a measured sign of how fast AI is entering mathematics, affecting authors, journals and hiring committees, though it counts only what authors choose to disclose and AI models helped classify the papers.
summary: Crypto Briefing reports, citing an analysis of arXiv math preprints published by the research group Epoch AI on 18 Sep 2026, that the share of papers acknowledging AI use rose from 4% in April 2026 to 25% in August, and that 6% credited AI with a substantive contribution, which Epoch likens to a co-author's role. The rise was sharpest in differential geometry, from about 8% to 57%; the figures measure what authors chose to disclose, and AI models were used to classify the papers, with human reviewers agreeing 93% of the time.
notes: Underlying analysis dated 18 Sep 2026; Crypto Briefing carried it on 9 Oct 2026.
